what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Hospital IT outage news reached only those already waiting
sections.para: At two London hospitals, staff said the IT systems were down, one waiting room was announced at about five hours, and a doctor called it national. Nothing checkable from home showed it. Northern Ireland and Wales publish live waits, but England has no equivalent, so a vault now logs it as a live local story.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Being there was the only way to find out
sections.para: Two sites, one trust, one message: systems down, about five hours' wait, possibly national. No trust notice, post, local story or dated search result showed it, and operational status channels need an NHS login. This is about the channel, not the staff; a vault now logs the evidence and an enquiry to the trust.

sections.label: What happened, separated by level
sections.line: Evidence supports a local outage; national scope stays unconfirmed
sections.para: Each item is labelled by level: staff statements at Charing Cross and Western Eye, a first-hand full waiting room, and a second-hand claim it was national. Both sites belong to Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, which shares a Cerner system across four trusts. Unrelated leads were ruled out by date, and national status portals needed logins.

sections.label: Newsworthy to me
sections.line: Knowing at lunchtime would have changed the day's decision
sections.para: The striking thing is not that IT failed, since staff handled it well, but that being there was the only way to know. Knowing earlier would have allowed going later, tomorrow or elsewhere. Nothing was hidden; the information is simply not news to newsrooms, not in scope for status pages, and nobody's job to publish.

sections.label: Where a local person could look, today
sections.line: Live hospital status is possible but England lacks it
sections.para: Northern Ireland publishes live median waits for every emergency department, Wales has My A&E Live, some English trusts publish waits, and Alberta recalculates every 2 minutes; England nationally offers only weekly or monthly figures, and Imperial nothing live. A wait number is not a disruption notice. The Civil Contingencies Act duty to warn likely does not reach this.

sections.label: Why the gap is wider now
sections.line: Local news and social feeds no longer carry this
sections.para: 4.4 million people live in local news deserts, London has about one outlet per 100,000 residents, and at least 293 local papers closed since 2005. Weekly X use for UK news is 10 per cent; local Facebook groups carry misinformation in about one in 26 posts, and genuine appeals get dismissed. Outage trackers only watch websites.

sections.label: Not naming and shaming
sections.line: Naming the trust is about the channel, not blame
sections.para: The trust is named only because the evidence is there. This is not a complaint about staff, not a claim the trust hid anything, and not a claim of a national NHS outage. The question applies to any trust, council or transport operator: where does a local person find out in time to plan?

sections.label: The vault, and what happens next
sections.line: A vault logs the incident by evidence level
sections.para: The Local evidence log keeps observations by level, claims with their status, every source and how it was accessed, leads that do not fit, and an enquiry to the trust's press office that the agent will send. A tool re-checks public sources on a schedule. More local stories will follow, like the Mill Street Bridge.

sections.label: What would close the gap
sections.line: Status lines, inside-out notices and persistent agents would help
sections.para: Four fixes: a plain status line for local services, a one-line public notice from whoever sends the internal bulletin, a log keeping reports with level, time and source, and an agent that keeps asking. Drafted from Dinis Cruz's memo on 8 October 2026; nobody has been contacted yet and the patient is deliberately not described.
